markets.rules_primary: If the Democratic minus Republican margin in the national House popular vote is at least 12 percentage points in the November 3, 2026 U.S. House general election, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary: The national House popular vote margin of victory shall be calculated as the vote percentage received by all Democratic party House candidates in the general election minus the vote percentage received by all Republican party House candidates in the general election. The margin will be positive if the Democratic party wins the national House popular vote and negative if they lose the national House popular vote.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?
markets.event_title: Alaska gas price tomorrow
markets.rules_primary: If the change in the average regular gasoline price for Alaska from the previous calendar day to Nov 21, 2026 is greater than or equal to 0.5 and less than 1.5 cents per gallon according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Alaska. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?
markets.event_title: Alabama gas price tomorrow
markets.rules_primary: If the change in the average regular gasoline price for Alabama from the previous calendar day to Nov 21, 2026 is greater than or equal to 0.5 and less than 1.5 cents per gallon according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Alabama. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?
markets.event_title: Arkansas gas price tomorrow
markets.rules_primary: If the change in the average regular gasoline price for Arkansas from the previous calendar day to Nov 21, 2026 is greater than or equal to 0.5 and less than 1.5 cents per gallon according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Arkansas. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Arkansas. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?

markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Arizona. markets.title: Will the highest 2024 Trump-minus-Harris presidential margin, in percentage points, among U.S. House districts won by a Democratic candidate be at least 22 at the November 3, 2026 general election?
markets.event_title: Reddest House district to elect a Democrat in 2026?
markets.rules_primary: If the highest 2024 Trump-minus-Harris presidential margin, in percentage points, among U.S. House districts won by a Democratic candidate is at least 22 at the November 3, 2026 general election, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A district's 2024 margin is Donald Trump's share of the 2024 presidential vote in that district minus Kamala Harris's share, as calculated by The Downballot in its 2024 presidential results by congressional district table, for the district boundaries in use at the 2026 elections, as shown in the table to one decimal place (the table lists Democratic minus Republican, so reverse its sign). Those margins are fixed as of Issuance and identified by state and district number, so later boundary changes and revisions to the table do NOT change them. The margin is negative where Harris won.

A district counts only if the candidate elected there at the November 3, 2026 general election, for the term beginning January 3, 2027, is listed on the ballot as a Democrat (including Minnesota's Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party), including as preferring the Democratic Party where a state uses an open, top-two or top-four ballot. If a runoff is required to determine the winner of any race, the runoff result governs. Independent and third-party winners do NOT count, even if they caucus with Democrats.

markets.title: Will the number of Democratic U.S. House members elected from the 235 districts that Donald Trump carried in 2024 be at least 58 at the November 3, 2026 general election?
markets.event_title: How many Trump-won districts will Democrats win in 2026?
markets.rules_primary: If the number of Democratic U.S. House members elected from the 235 districts that Donald Trump carried in 2024 is at least 58 at the November 3, 2026 general election, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The qualifying districts are the 235 in which Trump received more votes than Harris in 2024, as calculated by The Downballot in its 2024 presidential results by congressional district table, for the district boundaries in use at the 2026 elections. That list is fixed as of Issuance and identified by state and district number, so later boundary changes and revisions to the 2024 vote totals do NOT add or remove districts.

A district counts only if the candidate elected there at the November 3, 2026 general election, for the term beginning January 3, 2027, is listed on the ballot as a Democrat (including Minnesota's Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party), including as preferring the Democratic Party where a state uses an open, top-two or top-four ballot. If a runoff is required to determine the winner of any race, the runoff result governs. Independent and third-party winners do NOT count, even if they caucus with Democrats.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?
markets.event_title: Colorado gas price tomorrow
markets.rules_primary: If the change in the average regular gasoline price for Colorado from the previous calendar day to Nov 21, 2026 is greater than or equal to 0.5 and less than 1.5 cents per gallon according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Colorado. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.title: Will Chuck Schumer be reelected Senate Democratic leader for the 120th Congress by voice vote or acclamation?
markets.event_title: 120th Congress: Will Schumer be reelected by voice vote?
markets.rules_primary: If Chuck Schumer is reelected Senate Democratic leader for the 120th Congress by voice vote, acclamation or without objection before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Election as Senate Democratic leader means election to lead the Senate Democratic Caucus for the 120th Congress, whether the post is styled Democratic Leader or Majority Leader. The count is 1 if the Source Agencies report that Chuck Schumer was elected by voice vote, by acclamation or without objection, and 0 otherwise, including if no such election is held before Jan 1, 2027. An election by unanimous consent counts as an election without objection.

The following do NOT count:
An election in which senators cast ballots, whether secret or recorded, even if the result is unanimous
A ballot followed by a motion to make the result unanimous or to approve Chuck Schumer by acclamation
A report that Chuck Schumer was elected unanimously, or without opposition, that does not say the election was by voice vote, acclamation, without objection or by unanimous consent
A statement before the election about how it is expected to be held

If Source Agencies disagree on the method, a report by any Source Agency that a ballot was cast governs.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?
markets.event_title: Connecticut gas price tomorrow
markets.rules_primary: If the change in the average regular gasoline price for Connecticut from the previous calendar day to Nov 21, 2026 is greater than or equal to 0.5 and less than 1.5 cents per gallon according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Connecticut. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?
markets.event_title: Delaware gas price tomorrow
markets.rules_primary: If the change in the average regular gasoline price for Delaware from the previous calendar day to Nov 21, 2026 is greater than or equal to 0.5 and less than 1.5 cents per gallon according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Delaware. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.title: Will Schumer get at least 52 votes on the first Senate leader ballot?
markets.event_title: How many votes will Schumer get on the first Senate leader ballot?
markets.rules_primary: If the number of votes cast for Chuck Schumer on the first ballot in the Senate Democratic caucus election for its leader for the 120th Congress is at least 52 before Jan 3, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The first ballot is the first ballot held by the Senate Democratic caucus to elect its leader for the 120th Congress. The count is the number of votes cast for Chuck Schumer on it, as reported by a Source Agency.

If the caucus elects Chuck Schumer its leader without a ballot (for example by acclamation, voice vote or unanimous consent), the count is the number of senators and senators-elect in the Senate Democratic caucus, including independents who caucus with Democrats. A report that Chuck Schumer was elected unanimously that gives no number and does not say a ballot was held counts as an election without a ballot, unless a Source Agency reports that a ballot was held. The count is 0 if no ballot is held before Jan 3, 2027 and Chuck Schumer is not elected without one. If Chuck Schumer withdraws, the count is the number of votes cast for him on the first ballot, and 0 if none were cast.

Only an exact number reported by a Source Agency counts; a range, a margin or an approximate number does not. If a ballot is held but no Source Agency reports the number of votes cast for Chuck Schumer by the Expiration Date, the market resolves to the last fair price as solely determined by the Exchange. If Source Agencies report different counts, the count reported by the Source Agency listed first is used.

The following do NOT count:
Votes cast for Chuck Schumer on a later ballot
A motion or voice vote after a ballot to make the result unanimous
Votes cast for any other candidate, or abstentions

markets.rules_primary: If the change in the average regular gasoline price for Georgia from the previous calendar day to Nov 21, 2026 is greater than -0.5 and less than 0.5 cents per gallon according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Georgia. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.title: Will Van Hollen get at least 22 votes on the first Senate leader ballot?
markets.event_title: How many votes will Van Hollen get on the first Senate leader ballot?
markets.rules_primary: If the number of votes cast for Chris Van Hollen on the first ballot in the Senate Democratic caucus election for its leader for the 120th Congress is at least 22 before Jan 3, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The first ballot is the first ballot held by the Senate Democratic caucus to elect its leader for the 120th Congress. The count is the number of votes cast for Chris Van Hollen on it, as reported by a Source Agency.

The count is 0 if no ballot is held before Jan 3, 2027, including if the caucus elects its leader without one (for example by acclamation, voice vote or unanimous consent). A report that the leader was elected unanimously that gives no number and does not say a ballot was held counts as an election without a ballot, unless a Source Agency reports that a ballot was held. If Chris Van Hollen withdraws, the count is the number of votes cast for him on the first ballot, and 0 if none were cast.

Only an exact number reported by a Source Agency counts; a range, a margin or an approximate number does not. If a ballot is held but no Source Agency reports the number of votes cast for Chris Van Hollen by the Expiration Date, the market resolves to the last fair price as solely determined by the Exchange. If Source Agencies report different counts, the count reported by the Source Agency listed first is used.

The following do NOT count:
Votes cast for Chris Van Hollen on a later ballot
A motion or voice vote after a ballot to make the result unanimous
Votes cast for any other candidate, or abstentions

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?
markets.event_title: Hawaii gas price tomorrow
markets.rules_primary: If the change in the average regular gasoline price for Hawaii from the previous calendar day to Nov 21, 2026 is greater than or equal to 0.5 and less than 1.5 cents per gallon according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Hawaii. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?

The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Iowa. Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.title: Will the number of U.S. House seats won by Democratic Party candidates be at least 278 in the 2026 U.S. House elections?
markets.event_title: How many House seats will Democrats win in the Midterms?
markets.rules_primary: If the number of U.S. House seats won by Democratic Party candidates is at least 278 in the 2026 U.S. House elections, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A seat counts only if the relevant election authority records a Democratic designation for the winning candidate’s candidacy in the November 3, 2026 general election; a recognized state affiliate (including the Minnesota Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party and the North Dakota Democratic-Nonpartisan League Party), any one of several ballot lines, or a declared write-in candidacy so recorded all qualify. Caucus affiliation, endorsements and later party changes do not affect the count: a member elected without a Democratic designation who caucuses with Democrats is not counted, and one elected as a Democratic candidate who later leaves remains counted.

Only the regular general election in each of the 435 congressional districts for the term beginning January 3, 2027 counts; a special election for a 119th Congress vacancy is disregarded whenever held. No district counts twice.

Seats are counted from Designated Media Source calls as they stand at the Expiration time, not from House composition on any later date; the eight rank equally. A seat is counted when at least four have declared its winner with no contradictory declaration then outstanding; withdrawn or superseded declarations are disregarded. A seat not counted under that four-of-eight test is attributed to the candidate the state certifies as elected. A runoff seat is counted when that contest is called.

Designated Media Source declarations. For United States based elections, this Contract may be resolved on an accelerated basis if (A) at least four (4) of the eight (8) Designated Media Sources have declared a winning candidate, party, or option, and (B) none of the Designated Media Sources have issued a contradictory declaration. “Designated Media Sources” are: The New York Times (NYT), The Associated Press (AP), Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ), CNN, Fox News, NBC News, CBS News, and ABC News. Should one of the Designated Media Sources cease to provide independent election calls, it may be replaced at the sole discretion

markets.title: Will the number of Wisconsin State Senate seats held by Republicans be at least 22 after the November 3, 2026 general election?
markets.event_title: Where will Republicans win state legislative supermajorities in 2026?
markets.rules_primary: If the number of Wisconsin State Senate seats held by Republicans is at least 22 after the November 3, 2026 general election, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Each market counts the seats in that chamber held by the Republican Party when the chamber's November 3, 2026 general election results are certified. Every seat on the 2026 ballot is attributed to its certified winner, and every other seat to the party designation the state election authority recorded for the winner of that seat's most recent general or special election, regardless of any vacancy, appointment or party change since that election. The number shown is that state's constitutional requirement to override a governor's veto, applied to the chamber's full membership, including where the state measures it against members present and voting. Vacancies, appointments and party changes after certification, and special elections held after November 3, 2026, are disregarded.

A winner counts as Republican if the official results show the winner on the Republican Party's ballot line or, where they show a combined designation, list Republican first; a winner elected only on another party's line does not count.

Caucus affiliation, endorsements and later party changes do not affect the count: a member elected without a Republican designation who caucuses with Republicans is not counted, and one elected as a Republican candidate who later leaves remains counted.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?
markets.event_title: Kansas gas price tomorrow
markets.rules_primary: If the change in the average regular gasoline price for Kansas from the previous calendar day to Nov 21, 2026 is greater than or equal to 0.5 and less than 1.5 cents per gallon according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Kansas. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.title: Will a third-party Senate candidate win at least 4.5% of the vote in 2026?
markets.event_title: Highest third-party vote share in a 2026 Senate race?
markets.rules_primary: If the highest vote share received by any qualifying third-party candidate in a 2026 U.S. Senate election is at least 4.5% in the 2026 U.S. Senate elections, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A qualifying third-party candidate is a candidate recorded by the relevant state election authority under the name of a political party other than the Democratic Party, the Republican Party, or a recognized state affiliate of either (including the Minnesota Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party and the North Dakota Democratic-Nonpartisan League Party). A minor party whose registered name contains the word "Independent" (for example, the Alaskan Independence Party) qualifies. Candidates recorded as Independent, Unaffiliated, Nonaffiliated, Nonpartisan, Undeclared, No Party, No Party Preference, No Party Affiliation, or under any other non-party or petition label do not qualify. A candidate who is also the Democratic or Republican nominee does not qualify. A candidate nominated only by one or more qualifying parties qualifies, and their votes across all such lines are combined.

All U.S. Senate general elections held on November 3, 2026 are in scope, including special elections. Each qualifying candidate's figure is their share of all votes cast for that seat as certified by the relevant state election authority; in a ranked-choice contest, the first-round share is used. The market resolves on the single highest such certified share across all contests.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?

markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Kentucky. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?
markets.event_title: Louisiana gas price tomorrow
markets.rules_primary: If the change in the average regular gasoline price for Louisiana from the previous calendar day to Nov 21, 2026 is greater than or equal to 0.5 and less than 1.5 cents per gallon according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:

markets.title: Will Hakeem Jeffries be elected Speaker on the first ballot at the opening of the 120th Congress?
markets.event_title: 120th Congress: Will Jeffries be elected Speaker on the first ballot?
markets.rules_primary: If Hakeem Jeffries is elected Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives on the first ballot of the Speaker election at the opening of the 120th Congress before Feb 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The first ballot is the first roll-call vote for Speaker at the opening of the 120th Congress. The count is 1 if Hakeem Jeffries is declared elected Speaker on it, which requires a majority of the votes cast for a person by name, and 0 otherwise, including if no roll-call vote for Speaker is held before Feb 1, 2027.

The following do NOT count:
A later ballot on which Hakeem Jeffries is elected
A first ballot on which no candidate receives a majority, even if Hakeem Jeffries receives the most votes

The result is determined from the roll call record of the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?

markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Michigan. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.rules_secondary: The Clerk's official final record of the first roll call for Speaker governs. Votes recorded as Present or Not Voting, votes for anyone other than Hakeem Jeffries, and votes in a party caucus do NOT count. If the first roll call record shows no vote for Jeffries from the named person, including if they did not vote because they did not take their seat, the market resolves to No. A later ballot does not reopen it.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?

markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Minnesota. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.title: Will it be confirmed that Thomas Massie receives at least one vote for Speaker of the House on a roll call at the opening of the 120th Congress?
markets.event_title: 120th Congress: Who will get a vote for Speaker?
markets.rules_primary: If Thomas Massie receives at least one vote for Speaker of the House on a roll call at the opening of the 120th Congress after Issuance and before Feb 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This must be confirmed, verified, or established as factual by at least one Source Agency before Feb 1, 2027.

A person receives a vote when the roll call record of the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives, or a Source Agency report of that record, shows a vote cast for that person on a roll call to elect the Speaker at the opening of the 120th Congress. Every ballot held until a Speaker is elected counts, and one vote on any of them counts. A Member voting for themself counts, and so does a vote for a person who is not a Member of the House. If a Speaker is elected at the opening of the 120th Congress and the Clerk's record of those ballots shows no vote for this person, the market resolves to No once the Speaker is elected; a later report does not reopen it.

The following do NOT count:
A vote recorded as Present or Not Voting
A vote the Member changes before that ballot's result is announced
A vote for a name that does not identify this person alone, such as a surname shared by other Members, unless the record identifies them
A vote in a party caucus or conference election
A roll call to elect a Speaker after the opening of the Congress, such as to fill a vacancy
A pledge, petition, or statement of support without a recorded vote

markets.title: Will the 2026 House popular vote margin be within 0.9 points of the final VoteHub generic ballot margin?
markets.event_title: 2026 Midterms: House popular vote vs. generic ballot?
markets.rules_primary: If the national House popular vote margin (D − R) minus the VoteHub 2026 generic ballot margin (D − R, time-weighted) at 10:00 AM ET on November 3, 2026 is between -0.9 and 0.9 in the 2026 U.S. House general election, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary: The national House popular vote margin is the vote percentage received by all Democratic party House candidates minus the vote percentage received by all Republican party House candidates in the general election, as reported by the Clerk of the House, with each percentage taken over all votes cast; the margin is calculated from unrounded percentages and then rounded to one decimal place. The reference margin is the VoteHub 2026 generic congressional ballot margin (Democratic minus Republican, time-weighted) as displayed to one decimal place at 10:00 AM ET on November 3, 2026. The value is the national House popular vote margin minus the reference margin: positive if Democrats outperform the reference margin and negative if Republicans do. Each range includes both of its endpoints.

markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for North Carolina. markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?
markets.event_title: North Dakota gas price tomorrow
markets.rules_primary: If the change in the average regular gasoline price for North Dakota from the previous calendar day to Nov 21, 2026 is greater than or equal to 0.5 and less than 1.5 cents per gallon according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for North Dakota. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.rules_secondary: The Chamber of Deputies has 500 seats: 300 elected in single-member districts and 200 assigned by proportional representation. Seats count for Morena, the Labor Party (PT) and the Ecologist Green Party of Mexico (PVEM) as assigned to each party by the National Electoral Institute (INE) after the Jun 6, 2027 election, including district seats and proportional representation seats, as changed by any ruling of the Electoral Tribunal of the Federal Judiciary (TEPJF) on challenges. The three parties count whether they run in a coalition or separately. A district seat won by a coalition candidate counts for the party to which the INE attributes it. Later changes of party by a deputy do not count.

markets.title: Will the number of Knesset seats held by the factions in Israel's next government be at least 70 when the Knesset approves it before Oct 28, 2027 (0 if it does not)?
markets.event_title: How many Knesset seats will Israel's next government hold?
markets.rules_primary: If the number of Knesset seats held by the factions in Israel's next government is at least 70 when the Knesset approves it before Oct 28, 2027 (0 if it does not), then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Israel's next government is the first one the Knesset elected on Oct 27, 2026 approves in a vote of confidence. A faction counts if it is part of that government's coalition: it signed a coalition agreement to join the government that was submitted to the Knesset before the vote, or one of its members is a minister when the Knesset approves the government or is appointed a deputy minister within 30 days after the vote. Factions that only support the government from outside the coalition or abstain do not count, including under a written support agreement. Seats are each faction's size in the Knesset on the day of the vote; later changes do not count.

If that Knesset dissolves before approving a government, or none is approved before Oct 28, 2027, the number of seats is 0.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?
markets.event_title: New Hampshire gas price tomorrow
markets.rules_primary: If the change in the average regular gasoline price for New Hampshire from the previous calendar day to Nov 21, 2026 is greater than or equal to 0.5 and less than 1.5 cents per gallon according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for New Hampshire. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.title: Will Israel fail to form a government?
markets.event_title: What kind of government will Israel form?
markets.rules_primary: If the number of Knesset seats held by the factions in Israel's next government is exactly 0 when the Knesset approves it before Oct 28, 2027 (0 if it does not), then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Israel's next government is the first one the Knesset elected on Oct 27, 2026 approves in a vote of confidence. A faction counts if it is part of that government's coalition: it signed a coalition agreement to join the government that was submitted to the Knesset before the vote, or one of its members is a minister when the Knesset approves the government or is appointed a deputy minister within 30 days after the vote. Factions that only support the government from outside the coalition or abstain do not count, including under a written support agreement. Seats are each faction's size in the Knesset on the day of the vote; later changes do not count.

A majority government holds at least 61 of the 120 seats, and a minority government holds 1 to 60 ("between" includes both 1 and 60).

If that Knesset dissolves before approving a government, or none is approved before Oct 28, 2027, the number of seats is 0 and only No government resolves to Yes.

markets.title: Will the Democratic margin of victory in the 2026 U.S. House of Representatives national popular vote be between 8 and 10%?
markets.event_title: 2026 Midterms: House popular vote margin of victory? (Generic ballot)
markets.rules_primary: If the Democratic margin of victory in the 2026 U.S. House of Representatives national popular vote is between 8 and 10 percentage points, inclusive of its lower bound and exclusive of its upper bound, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary: The national House popular vote margin of victory shall be calculated as the vote percentage received by all Democratic party House candidates in the general election minus the vote percentage received by all Republican party House candidates in the general election. The margin will be positive if the Democratic party wins the national House popular vote and negative if they lose the national House popular vote. Each margin range is inclusive of its lower bound and exclusive of its upper bound. No rounding shall be applied to the calculated margin. For example, for consecutive ranges of 5-6% and 6-7%, a margin of 5.99999% resolves within the 5-6% range, while a margin of exactly 6% resolves within the 6-7% range.

markets.rules_secondary: The national House popular vote margin of victory shall be calculated as the vote percentage received by all Democratic party House candidates in the general election minus the vote percentage received by all Republican party House candidates in the general election. The margin will be positive if the Democratic party wins the national House popular vote and negative if they lose the national House popular vote. Each margin range is inclusive of its lower bound and exclusive of its upper bound. No rounding shall be applied to the calculated margin. For example, for consecutive ranges of 5-6% and 6-7%, a margin of 5.99999% resolves within the 5-6% range, while a margin of exactly 6% resolves within the 6-7% range.

markets.title: Will the number of candidates who participate in the first debate officially sanctioned by the Democratic National Committee (DNC) as a 2028 Democratic presidential primary debate be at least 8 before Mar 1, 2028?
markets.event_title: How many Democrats will be in the first 2028 primary debate?
markets.rules_primary: If the number of candidates who participate in the first debate officially sanctioned by the Democratic National Committee (DNC) as a 2028 Democratic presidential primary debate is at least 8 before Mar 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A debate counts when it is officially sanctioned by the Democratic National Committee (DNC) as a 2028 Democratic presidential primary debate and at least two candidates for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination participate together.
The first debate is the earliest debate that counts.
A debate held over more than one night, or in more than one stage on the same day (such as a main debate and an earlier undercard), is one debate. Each candidate who participates in any night or stage counts once.
A candidate who is invited or qualifies but does not participate is not counted.
If no debate counts before Mar 1, 2028, the number is 0.
The following do NOT count:
Forums, town halls or other events where candidates appear one at a time
Debates not sanctioned by the DNC
Candidates who participate only in a later debate

markets.title: Will the number of candidates who participate in the first RNC-sanctioned 2028 Republican presidential primary debate be at least 2 before Mar 1, 2028?
markets.event_title: How many Republicans will be in the first 2028 primary debate?
markets.rules_primary: If the number of candidates who participate in the first RNC-sanctioned 2028 Republican presidential primary debate is at least 2 before Mar 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
An RNC-sanctioned debate is a debate officially sanctioned by the Republican National Committee (RNC) as a 2028 Republican presidential primary debate. The first one is the earliest such debate in which at least two candidates for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination participate together.

A debate held over more than one night, or in more than one stage on the same day (such as a main debate and an earlier undercard), is one debate. Every candidate who participates in any night or stage is counted once. Later debates do NOT change the number.

The following do NOT count:

Announcing or scheduling a debate that has not taken place
Forums, town halls or other events where candidates appear one at a time
Debates not sanctioned by the RNC

If no such debate takes place before Mar 1, 2028, the number is 0.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?
markets.event_title: New York gas price tomorrow
markets.rules_primary: If the change in the average regular gasoline price for New York from the previous calendar day to Nov 21, 2026 is greater than or equal to 0.5 and less than 1.5 cents per gallon according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for New York. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.

markets.title: Will a 2028 Democratic presidential primary or caucus be won with under 25% of the vote?
markets.event_title: Will the 2028 Democratic presidential primary be fractured?
markets.rules_primary: If the lowest winning vote share in any state's 2028 Democratic presidential primary or caucus is below 25% in the final round of counting, for contests held before Sep 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Each state's contest is the statewide primary or caucus that allocates the most Democratic national convention delegates from that state (the earlier one if two allocate the same number), except that in New Hampshire it is the primary run by the Secretary of State and in Iowa it is the first statewide preference vote the Iowa Democratic Party reports, whether or not the Democratic National Committee sanctions either. The 50 states and the District of Columbia are in scope; territories and Democrats Abroad are not.

The winner of a contest is the candidate with the most votes in its final round of counting, such as the final alignment of a caucus or the last round of a ranked-choice count. "Uncommitted" and similar ballot options are not candidates and cannot be the winner.

The winner's vote share is their votes divided by all votes counted in that final round, including votes for "Uncommitted" and other ballot options, calculated from the reported totals without rounding. Resolution is based on certified results only, not preliminary results; for a contest run by a party, the party's official reported results are used.

A contest that is not held by Aug 31, 2028, or that reports no statewide vote count, is not counted.

markets.title: Will gas prices show a small increase?
markets.event_title: Ohio gas price tomorrow
markets.rules_primary: If the change in the average regular gasoline price for Ohio from the previous calendar day to Nov 21, 2026 is greater than or equal to 0.5 and less than 1.5 cents per gallon according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The daily change is calculated by subtracting the previous calendar day's average regular gasoline price from the average regular gasoline price for Nov 21, 2026, using AAA's figures for Ohio. The difference is multiplied by 100 to express the change in cents per gallon. Positive values indicate increases; negative values indicate decreases.

Use the first published price for each date at the source's full published precision, without rounding either price or the calculated change. The numerical condition determines the outcome; labels such as “small” and “large” are descriptive.
